category: Pipe Flow Module: Pipe Networks, Water Hammer, Nonisothermal and Reacting Pipe Flow, Fittings and Couplings
description: 1D pipe network modeling with the COMSOL Pipe Flow Module: Nonisothermal Pipe Flow, Water Hammer, Reacting Pipe Flow, Heat Transfer in Pipes and Transport of Diluted Species in Pipes, pipe properties and friction factor correlations, point features for bends, valves, control and 3-way valves, orifices, pumps, junctions and pressure locks, wall heat transfer layers, and couplings to 3D flow and heat transfer, with verified Java type ids and property names (COMSOL 6.4).

tools.name: Nonisothermal Pipe Flow (nipfl)
tools.description: Predefined 1D interface computing pressure, cross-section-averaged velocity and temperature along pipe edges in 2D/3D, combining Pipe Flow and Heat Transfer in Pipes with temperature-dependent properties, wall heat exchange, pressure work and friction heating. It is used for district heating networks, geothermal loops, cooling channels in molds and insulated pipelines.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Nonisothermal Flow > Nonisothermal Pipe Flow (nipfl); Java: physics().create("nipfl", "NonisothermalPipeFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Fluid model
parameters.description: Newtonian, power law, Bingham or Herschel–Bulkley.

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Fluid (fluid1), Pipe Properties (pipe1), Pressure (pr1), Temperature (temp1), Initial Values.

parameters.name: Wall Heat Transfer
parameters.description: Film resistances and wall layers to the surroundings.

tools.notes: Requires the Pipe Flow Module. Verified id NonisothermalPipeFlow (NonisothermalFlowInPipes is an alternative registered id).

tools.name: Water Hammer (whtd)
tools.description: Time-dependent 1D interface for hydraulic transients (water hammer) in elastic pipe systems: linearized compressibility of fluid and pipe wall gives pressure waves traveling at the pipe-modified speed of sound, with friction losses. It predicts pressure surges from fast valve closure or pump trips in water mains, oil lines and cooling systems.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Water Hammer (whtd); Java: physics().create("whtd", "WaterHammer", "geom1")

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Fluid Properties (fp1), Pipe Properties (pipe1), Closed (closed1), Initial Values.

parameters.name: Boundary nodes
parameters.description: Velocity (Source), Pressure, Closed.

parameters.name: Local Friction Loss
parameters.description: Lumped losses at points.

tools.notes: Requires the Pipe Flow Module. Resolve the wave with a mesh and time step satisfying c·Δt ≈ Δx.

tools.name: Reacting Pipe Flow (rpfl)
tools.description: Multiphysics 1D interface combining Pipe Flow, Heat Transfer in Pipes and Transport of Diluted Species in Pipes to compute flow, temperature and concentrations of reacting species along pipes and channels, e.g., tubular reactors, chlorine decay in water networks and heat-exchanger reactors.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Reacting Pipe Flow (rpfl); Java: physics().create("rpfl", "ReactingPipeFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Fluid, Pipe Properties, Temperature, Pressure, Concentration, Initial Values.

parameters.name: Reactions
parameters.description: Reaction rates for each species (and heat of reaction).

tools.notes: Requires the Pipe Flow Module; multiple species may require additional chemistry licenses.

tools.name: Heat Transfer in Pipes (htp, Pipe Flow Module)
tools.description: 1D energy balance along pipe edges with known velocity and pressure, including axial conduction, convection, heat sources and wall heat exchange through internal/external film resistances and multilayer walls. It is used alone when the flow is prescribed or coupled to Pipe Flow (Nonisothermal Pipe Flow) and to 3D solids via Pipe Wall Heat Transfer.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Heat Transfer in Pipes (htp); Java: physics().create("htp", "HeatTransferPipes", "geom1")

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Heat Transfer, Pipe Properties, Temperature, Initial Values.

parameters.name: Velocity field
parameters.description: User defined or from Pipe Flow.

parameters.name: Wall Heat Transfer
parameters.description: External temperature and film/wall resistance subnodes.

tools.notes: Requires the Pipe Flow Module.

tools.name: Transport of Diluted Species in Pipes (dsp)
tools.description: 1D mass balance for solutes in pipes including convection, diffusion, Taylor dispersion and reactions, with wall mass transfer to the surroundings and junction mixing; multiple species depending on licenses. Typical uses are tracer transport, water quality and contaminant spreading in pipe networks.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Transport of Diluted Species in Pipes (dsp); Java: physics().create("dsp", "DilutedSpeciesPipes", "geom1")

parameters.name: Convection and Diffusion
parameters.description: Velocity (from Pipe Flow) and diffusion/dispersion coefficients.

parameters.name: Reactions
parameters.description: Rate expressions per species.

parameters.name: Boundary nodes
parameters.description: Concentration, Mass Outflow, Open Pipe End, Junction.

tools.notes: Requires the Pipe Flow Module.

tools.name: Fluid Models in Pipe Flow (Newtonian, Gas–Liquid, Power Law, Bingham, Herschel–Bulkley)
tools.description: Interface-level Fluid model setting of Pipe Flow: Newtonian single phase (default), Newtonian gas–liquid mixtures using a friction factor multiplier or an effective Reynolds number (adds a Phase Fractions node), and non-Newtonian power law, Bingham plastic or Herschel–Bulkley fluids with dedicated friction correlations. Compressible flow and gas properties are handled through the material and reference settings.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow (pfl) > Fluid Model; Java: physics().create("pfl", "FlowInPipes", "geom1")

parameters.name: Fluid model
parameters.description: Newtonian | Power Law | Bingham | Herschel-Bulkley.

parameters.name: Newtonian option
parameters.description: Single phase | Gas-Liquid, friction factor multiplier | Gas-Liquid, effective Reynolds number.

parameters.name: Gas–liquid viscosity model
parameters.description: einstein | linear | reciprocal | liquid | user (Fluid Properties gasliquidviscositymodel).

tools.notes: In 6.4 the Pipe Flow Java id is FlowInPipes (PipeFlow remains for backward compatibility).

tools.name: Fluid Properties (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Always-present edge node adding the momentum and mass balance of Pipe Flow and defining density and dynamic viscosity (from material or user) or, for gas–liquid models, liquid and gas materials and a mixture viscosity model; for non-Newtonian fluids the consistency and flow index (power law), yield stress and plastic viscosity (Bingham) are entered here.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > Fluid Properties (fp1); Java: physics("pfl").feature("fp1").set("rho", ...)

parameters.name: rho / mu (rho_mat, mu_mat)
parameters.description: Density and viscosity (default 1e3 kg/m³, 1e-3 Pa·s when user defined).

parameters.name: n / m / srref
parameters.description: Power-law index, consistency and reference shear rate.

parameters.name: tauB / muB
parameters.description: Bingham yield stress and plastic viscosity.

parameters.name: rholiq, muliq, rhogas, mugas
parameters.description: Gas–liquid phase properties.

tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Pipe Properties (Pipe Flow): Shape and Flow Resistance
tools.description: Edge node defining the pipe cross section (circular, square, rectangular, concentric annular or user-defined area and wetted perimeter), the wall friction model for the Darcy friction factor and the surface roughness. Several Pipe Properties nodes give different diameters or materials to different branches of a network.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > Pipe Properties (pipe1); Java: physics("pfl").feature("pipe1").set("shape", "Round"); set("innerd", ...)

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: NotSet | Round | Square | Rectangular | ConcentricCircularAnnular | UserDefined (Aww, Zww).

parameters.name: innerd / innerw / innerh / di_outer / do_inner
parameters.description: Dimensions (default inner diameter 10 cm).

parameters.name: frictionmodel
parameters.description: Numeric code; default (0) is Churchill; others Stokes, Wood, Haaland, Colebrook, von Karman, Swamee-Jain, user defined (f).

parameters.name: roughness / e
parameters.description: Preset surface roughness (drawn tubing default) or user roughness e.

tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4 (shape, innerd, frictionmodel, roughness, e).

tools.name: Friction Factor Models: Churchill, Haaland, Colebrook, Swamee–Jain, von Kármán, Wood, Stokes
tools.description: Darcy friction factor correlations of the Pipe Flow interfaces for Newtonian fluids: Churchill (default, valid over laminar, transitional and turbulent regimes), Stokes (laminar 64/Re), Wood, Haaland (explicit Colebrook approximation), Colebrook (implicit), von Kármán (fully rough) and Swamee–Jain; the roughness-dependent models use preset surface roughness values from smooth (0 mm) and drawn tubing (0.0015 mm) to commercial steel (0.046 mm), cast iron (0.26 mm), concrete (1.5 mm) and riveted steel (4.5 mm).
tools.usage: Pipe Properties > Flow Resistance > Friction model; Surface Roughness list

parameters.name: Churchill
parameters.description: Continuous over all Re; recommended default.

parameters.name: Colebrook / Haaland / Swamee–Jain
parameters.description: Turbulent flow with roughness.

parameters.name: Surface roughness presets
parameters.description: Smooth, Drawn tubing, Glass, Thermoplastics, Commercial steel, Wrought iron, Steel welded seamless, Asphalted cast iron, Galvanized iron, Cast iron, Wood stave, Copper and brass, Concrete, Riveted steel, User defined.

tools.example:
// GUI: Pipe Properties 1 > Friction model = Colebrook; Surface roughness = Galvanized iron (0.15 mm)
// Pressure drop per length: dp/dx = f_D * rho*u^2/(2*d_h)
tools.notes: Stokes applies only to laminar flow; Churchill blends laminar and turbulent regimes smoothly, which helps convergence.

tools.name: Non-Newtonian Pipe Friction Models: Irvine, Darby, Swamee–Aggarwal
tools.description: Friction factor correlations for non-Newtonian fluids in circular pipes: Irvine or Stokes for power-law fluids, Darby for Bingham plastics, and Swamee–Aggarwal for Herschel–Bulkley fluids; user-defined Darcy friction factors are available for all and required for noncircular cross sections. They enable slurry, drilling mud and food-product pipeline design.
tools.usage: Pipe Properties > Flow Resistance (with Fluid model Power Law, Bingham or Herschel–Bulkley)

parameters.name: Power law
parameters.description: Irvine, Stokes, User defined (frictionmodelP).

parameters.name: Bingham
parameters.description: Darby or User defined (frictionmodelB).

parameters.name: Herschel–Bulkley
parameters.description: swameeAggarwal or userDef (frictionmodelHB).

tools.example:
// GUI: Pipe Flow > Fluid Model = Herschel-Bulkley; Pipe Properties > Friction model = Swamee-Aggarwal
model.component("comp1").physics("pfl").feature("pipe1").set("frictionmodelHB", "swameeAggarwal");
tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Phase Fractions (Gas–Liquid Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Edge node added for the gas–liquid Newtonian fluid models of Pipe Flow, specifying the gas content as area-averaged void fraction or quality (mass fraction). Combined with the friction factor multiplier or effective Reynolds number models it estimates two-phase pressure drop in pipelines and heat exchangers.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow (Gas-Liquid fluid model) > Phase Fractions (phf1)

parameters.name: Gas fraction specification
parameters.description: Area averaged void fraction ϕ_G or Quality ω_G.

tools.example: // GUI: Pipe Flow > Fluid Model = Newtonian, Gas-Liquid, friction factor multiplier; Phase Fractions 1 > Quality = 0.05
tools.notes: Homogeneous two-phase approach; slip and flow regimes are not resolved.

tools.name: Section Orientation and Volume Force (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Section Orientation (3D subnode of Pipe Properties) defines the orientation of noncircular cross sections via a reference point or orientation vector, needed when coupling to pipe mechanics or for results rendering; Volume Force adds a force per volume along the pipe, e.g., gravity in inclined or vertical pipes.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > Pipe Properties > Section Orientation (PipeSectionOrientation); Pipe Flow > Volume Force (VolumeForce)

parameters.name: Orientation
parameters.description: Reference point or orientation vector (3D).

parameters.name: Volume force F
parameters.description: N/m³, e.g., {0,0,-pfl.rho*g_const}.

tools.notes: Only the component along the pipe tangent affects the 1D momentum balance.

tools.name: Inlet (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Point condition at pipe ends specifying the inflow as mass flow rate (default), velocity, volumetric flow rate, standard flow (SCCM), a pump curve against an external pressure, or a reservoir with density, pressure and entrance loss (projecting, sharp edged, rounded or user loss coefficient). Outflow through an Inlet is not prevented mathematically.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > Inlet; Java: physics("pfl").create("inl1", "Inlet", 0); feature("inl1").set("qm0", ...)

parameters.name: spec
parameters.description: Specification code (default mass flow rate); options Mass flow rate, Velocity, Volumetric flow rate, Standard flow SCCM, Pump, Reservoir.

parameters.name: qm0 / u0 / qv0 / qsccm0
parameters.description: Values for each specification.

parameters.name: pext / PumpCurve
parameters.description: Pump option: external pressure and pump curve (data or user).

parameters.name: pres / rhores / entrancetype
parameters.description: Reservoir pressure, density and entrance type.

tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4. Specify a pressure at one end of each flow path.

tools.name: Outlet, Pressure and No Flow (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: End-point conditions of pipe networks: Outlet prescribes outflow as mass flow, velocity or volumetric flow (same options as Inlet); Pressure fixes the pressure at a point connected to exactly one edge (default 101325 Pa); No Flow plugs an exit or inlet.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > Outlet (Outlet) / Pressure (Pressure) / No Flow (NoFlow); Java: physics("pfl").create("pr2", "Pressure", 0)

parameters.name: p0
parameters.description: Boundary pressure (Pressure node).

parameters.name: Outlet specification
parameters.description: As for Inlet.

tools.notes: The default Pressure node pr1 is created on free pipe ends.

tools.name: Lossless Fitting (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Default point condition imposed at all junction points that connects pipe segments without pressure loss; it is overridden wherever Bend, Valve, Contraction/Expansion, Pump or junction nodes are applied to the same points.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > Lossless Fitting (lf1, default)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: All junction points by default.

tools.notes: Add explicit fittings where minor losses matter.

tools.name: Bend (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Point feature adding the lumped pressure loss Δp = K ρ u²/2 of a pipe bend between exactly two edges: 90° standard elbow (K = 0.9, default), 45° standard elbow (K = 0.5), a user loss coefficient or a user pressure drop.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > Bend; Java: physics("pfl").create("bend1", "Bend", 0)

parameters.name: bendtype
parameters.description: Code: 90° elbow (default), 45° elbow, user loss coefficient (K), user pressure drop (dp).

tools.notes: Loss coefficients follow standard turbulent-flow tables.

tools.name: Valve (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Point feature adding a fixed valve loss between two pipe edges: globe (K = 10, default), angle (4.4), gate (0.2), ball (4.5), butterfly (0.6), swing check (2.5), user loss coefficient or user pressure drop, for fully open valves.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > Valve; Java: physics("pfl").create("valve1", "Valve", 0)

parameters.name: valvetype
parameters.description: Code for globe, angle, gate, ball, butterfly, swing check, user K, user Δp.

parameters.name: K / dp
parameters.description: User loss coefficient or pressure drop.

tools.notes: Use Control Valve for partially open or regulating valves.

tools.name: Control Valve (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Point feature for a regulating valve with an opening fraction and a flow characteristic (linear, equal percentage or quick opening), specified by loss coefficient range (K_min open to K_max closed), flow coefficient C_v, flow factor K_v or a target flow rate. It supports control studies and events that adjust valve opening.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > Control Valve; Java: physics("pfl").create("cntvalve1", "ControlValve", 0)

parameters.name: valveSpecification
parameters.description: lossCoefficient | flowCoefficient | flowFactor | flowrate.

parameters.name: flowCharacteristic
parameters.description: Linear | EqualPercentage (rangeability R) | QuickOpening.

parameters.name: xfr
parameters.description: Opening fraction (1 = fully open).

parameters.name: Kmin / Kmax / Cvmax / Kvmax
parameters.description: Loss/flow coefficients.

tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4 (new valve features in 6.3/6.4).

tools.name: 3-Way Valve (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Point feature at a junction of exactly three edges that mixes two inlet streams into one outlet or splits one stream into two, with a main branch and two side branches whose opening follows the opening fraction and flow characteristic; specified by loss coefficient, flow coefficient or flow factor. Used for thermostatic mixing and diverter valves in heating loops.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > 3-Way Valve; Java: physics("pfl").create("threewvalve1", "ThreeWayValve", 0)

parameters.name: Main branch
parameters.description: Edge where flow is always present.

parameters.name: Opening fraction x_fr
parameters.description: 1 directs all flow to Side Branch 1; Switch branch option.

parameters.name: Specification
parameters.description: Loss coefficient, flow coefficient or flow factor.

tools.notes: Two 3-way valves cannot sit on both endpoints of the same edge.

tools.name: Contraction/Expansion (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Point feature adding the loss of a change in pipe cross section between two segments: sudden (K = 0.5(1-β²) for contraction, (1-β²)² for expansion), gradual with an angle of convergence, or user loss coefficient, where β is the diameter ratio.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > Contraction/Expansion; Java: physics("pfl").create("contr1", "ContractionExpansion", 0)

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Sudden (default), Gradual (angle alpha) or User loss coefficient (K).

tools.notes: The adjacent Pipe Properties must define different diameters.

tools.name: Orifice (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Point feature for an orifice plate between two segments, sharp edged or round edged (with edge radius), with the pressure loss computed from the orifice-to-pipe diameter ratio. Used for flow metering and restriction design.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > Orifice; Java: physics("pfl").create("orif1", "Orifice", 0)

parameters.name: OrificeType
parameters.description: sharp (default) or round.

parameters.name: d_o / r_o
parameters.description: Orifice diameter and edge radius.

tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Pump (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Point feature between two edges representing a pump by fixed mass flow rate (default), downstream pressure, pressure increase or a pump curve (head versus volumetric flow rate from data or user expression); the pump direction is set along a coordinate axis. It drives circulation loops and sizes pumps against system curves.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > Pump; Java: physics("pfl").create("pump1", "Pump", 0)

parameters.name: pumptype
parameters.description: Code: Fixed flow rate (default), Downstream pressure (pdown), Pressure increase (deltap), Pump curve.

parameters.name: massflowrate
parameters.description: Mass flow for fixed-flow pumps.

parameters.name: direction3D
parameters.description: X+, X-, Y+, Y-, Z+, Z- (pressure increases in this direction).

parameters.name: PumpCurve / spcd / V0data
parameters.description: Pump curve data table or user-defined head.

tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: T-Junction (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Point feature for a junction of two collinear main branches and one perpendicular side branch acting as split or merger, with turbulent losses from main/side loss coefficients (defaults 0.1 and 1.2), common-mode or extended coefficient sets, or specified pressure drops. T-junction points can be found automatically.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > T-Junction; Java: physics("pfl").create("tjunc1", "Tjunction", 0)

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: kfactors (Kmain, Kside) | kfactorcom | kfactorsext | pdrops.

parameters.name: selectionControl
parameters.description: Automatic search (0) or manual selection (1).

parameters.name: angletol
parameters.description: Angle tolerance for collinearity.

tools.notes: A warning is issued if the branch geometry does not match a T; use n-Way Junction otherwise.

tools.name: Y-Junction and n-Way Junction (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Point features for other junction geometries: Y-Junction handles one main and two symmetric side branches (equal angles, not 120°) with main/side loss coefficients or pressure drops; n-Way Junction handles any number of connected pipes at arbitrary angles with a loss coefficient per branch.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > Y-Junction (Yjunction) / n-Way Junction (NJunction); Java: physics("pfl").create("yjunc1", "Yjunction", 0)

parameters.name: Loss coefficients
parameters.description: Main and side (Y) or per branch (n-way).

parameters.name: Manual control of selections
parameters.description: Automatic junction search can be overridden.

tools.notes: For Nonisothermal and Reacting Pipe Flow the junction pressure drop formula accounts for density.

tools.name: Internal Pressure Lock (Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Point feature fixing the pressure at an internal point connecting exactly two edges, used to set the pressure level of closed loops (e.g., circulation circuits without free ends) where no boundary pressure exists.
tools.usage: Pipe Flow > Internal Pressure Lock; Java: physics("pfl").create("ipl1", "PressureLock", 0)

parameters.name: Pressure
parameters.description: Pressure value at the locked point.

tools.notes: Java type id PressureLock (GUI label Internal Pressure Lock).

tools.name: Pipe Properties and Pipe Models (Water Hammer)
tools.description: Water Hammer version of Pipe Properties adding the pipe model that sets the effective wave speed from wall elasticity: zero axial stress (default), anchored at one end, anchored at both ends (Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, wall thickness) or incompressible cross section, plus the usual shape and friction settings.
tools.usage: Water Hammer > Pipe Properties (pipe1)

parameters.name: Pipe model
parameters.description: Zero axial stress | Anchored at one end | Anchored at both ends | Incompressible cross section.

parameters.name: E / ν / Δw
parameters.description: Wall Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio and thickness.

parameters.name: Flow resistance
parameters.description: Friction model as in Pipe Flow.

tools.example: // GUI: Water Hammer > Pipe Properties 1 > Pipe model = Anchored at both ends; E = 200[GPa], nu = 0.3, wall thickness = 5[mm]
tools.notes: Stiffer pipes give faster waves and higher surge pressures (Joukowsky Δp = ρ c Δu).

tools.name: Local Friction Loss, Closed, Velocity and Pressure (Water Hammer)
tools.description: Point features of the Water Hammer interface: Local Friction Loss adds a lumped loss with coefficient K_f; Closed imposes zero velocity (closed valve, dead end); Velocity prescribes the velocity (e.g., a valve closure ramp); Pressure prescribes the pressure (reservoir).
tools.usage: Water Hammer > Local Friction Loss (FrictionLoss) / Closed (Closed) / Velocity (Source) / Pressure (Pressure)

parameters.name: K_f
parameters.description: Loss coefficient (Local Friction Loss).

parameters.name: u_in
parameters.description: Velocity value or ramp expression.

parameters.name: p0
parameters.description: Pressure value.

tools.notes: Java type ids from the COMSOL 6.4 plugin registry (the Velocity node is type Source).

tools.name: Fluid and Heat Transfer Nodes (Nonisothermal Pipe Flow)
tools.description: Edge nodes of Nonisothermal Pipe Flow: Fluid defines density, viscosity, heat capacity, ratio of specific heats and thermal conductivity and optionally includes pressure work for compressible fluids with large pressure drops; the Heat Transfer node covers non-Newtonian (Bingham-type) property input with yield stress and plastic viscosity.
tools.usage: Nonisothermal Pipe Flow > Fluid (fluid1) / Heat Transfer

parameters.name: Include pressure work
parameters.description: Adds pressure-volume work to the energy balance.

parameters.name: Cp / γ / k
parameters.description: Heat capacity, ratio of specific heats, thermal conductivity.

parameters.name: Yield stress / plastic viscosity
parameters.description: Bingham properties (Heat Transfer node).

tools.example:
// GUI: Nonisothermal Pipe Flow > Fluid 1 > Include pressure work = on (gas pipelines)
model.component("comp1").physics("nipfl").feature("fluid1");
tools.notes: Properties default to From material.

tools.name: Wall Heat Transfer (Heat Transfer in Pipes)
tools.description: Edge node setting heat exchange across the pipe wall to an external temperature (user value or averaged from an adjacent 3D domain via Pipe Wall Heat Transfer), with the overall resistance built from subnodes: Internal Film Resistance (required), Wall Layer(s) and External Film Resistance.
tools.usage: Heat Transfer in Pipes / Nonisothermal Pipe Flow > Wall Heat Transfer; Java: physics("htp").create("wht1", "WallHeatTransfer", 1)

parameters.name: External temperature T_ext
parameters.description: User defined; clear Take average in adjacent domain for edge-local expressions.

parameters.name: Subnodes
parameters.description: Internal Film Resistance, Wall Layer, External Film Resistance.

tools.notes: At least an Internal Film Resistance subnode is required (a drilled channel in a solid).

tools.name: Internal Film Resistance (Heat Transfer in Pipes)
tools.description: Subnode of Wall Heat Transfer computing the inside convective film coefficient from a Nusselt number: Automatic (laminar Nu = 3.66 or turbulent correlations depending on Reynolds and Prandtl numbers) or a user-defined Nusselt number.
tools.usage: Wall Heat Transfer > Internal Film Resistance

parameters.name: Internal film resistance model
parameters.description: Automatic or User defined Nusselt number (default 3.66).

tools.example: // GUI: Wall Heat Transfer 1 > Internal Film Resistance 1 > Automatic
tools.notes: The automatic correlation switches regimes with the local Reynolds number.

tools.name: External Film Resistance and Wall Layer (Heat Transfer in Pipes)
tools.description: Subnodes of Wall Heat Transfer: External Film Resistance adds forced convection (with external fluid velocity), natural convection or a user heat transfer coefficient on the outer pipe surface using the surrounding fluid properties; Wall Layer adds conduction resistance of a wall or insulation layer (thermal conductivity and thickness), with multiple layers allowed.
tools.usage: Wall Heat Transfer > External Film Resistance / Wall Layer

parameters.name: External film heat transfer model
parameters.description: External forced convection (default), External natural convection, User defined.

parameters.name: Surrounding fluid
parameters.description: Material and properties of the outside fluid (not the pipe fluid).

parameters.name: Wall Layer k / Δw
parameters.description: Thermal conductivity and thickness per layer.

tools.example: // GUI: Wall Heat Transfer 1 > add Wall Layer (steel 5 mm, k = 45 W/(m*K)), Wall Layer (insulation 50 mm, k = 0.04), External Film Resistance (forced convection, air at 5 m/s)
tools.notes: Select the correct surrounding material in External Film Resistance; the domain material is usually the pipe fluid.

tools.name: Open Pipe End and Heat Outflow (Heat Transfer in Pipes)
tools.description: Point conditions for pipe ends in heat transfer: Open Pipe End supports reversible flow, applying a Danckwerts inflow condition with an upstream temperature for incoming flow and zero conductive flux for outgoing flow; Heat Outflow states that only convective heat leaves through an outlet.
tools.usage: Heat Transfer in Pipes > Open Pipe End / Heat Outflow

parameters.name: Upstream temperature T_ustr
parameters.description: Temperature outside the open end (Open Pipe End).

tools.example: // GUI: Nonisothermal Pipe Flow > Open Pipe End 1 at points where flow direction may reverse; T_ustr = 283[K]
tools.notes: Use Temperature at pure inlets and Heat Outflow at pure outlets.

tools.name: Wall Mass Transfer and Junction (Transport of Diluted Species in Pipes)
tools.description: Features of Transport of Diluted Species in Pipes: Wall Mass Transfer models species loss to the surroundings through a permeable or absorbing wall with a mass transfer coefficient and bulk concentration; Junction mixes species at fittings with three or more pipes, prescribing flow-weighted inflow concentrations to outgoing branches and outflow conditions to incoming ones.
tools.usage: Transport of Diluted Species in Pipes > Wall Mass Transfer (edges) / Junction (points)

parameters.name: k_wall,c
parameters.description: Mass transfer coefficient per species (m/s).

parameters.name: c_bulk
parameters.description: External bulk concentration.

parameters.name: Junction
parameters.description: Assumes negligible junction hold-up volume.

tools.example: // GUI: Transport of Diluted Species in Pipes > Wall Mass Transfer 1: k = 1e-6[m/s], c_bulk = 0
tools.notes: Junctions support flow reversal in each branch.

tools.name: Pipe Connection (Pipe Flow to 3D Flow Coupling)
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling linking a 1D Pipe Flow end point to an inlet/outlet boundary of a 3D laminar or RANS-EVM flow domain, exchanging flow rate and pressure (and, with Heat Transfer and Heat Transfer in Pipes selected, temperature). It lets detailed 3D components be embedded in large pipe networks.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Pipe Connection (3D components); select Fluid flow and Pipe flow interfaces, the 3D boundary and the pipe point

parameters.name: Boundary selection, fluid
parameters.description: 3D inlet/outlet face.

parameters.name: Point selection, pipe
parameters.description: Pipe end point.

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Fluid flow, Pipe flow, optional Heat transfer and Heat transfer in pipes.

tools.notes: Available for 3D only; the flow side must be laminar or a RANS eddy-viscosity model.

tools.name: Pipe Wall Heat Transfer (Multiphysics Coupling)
tools.description: Edge coupling between a 3D (or 2D) heat transfer domain and pipe edges modeled with Heat Transfer in Pipes or Nonisothermal Pipe Flow: the pipe's wall heat exchange Q_wall is applied as a line source averaged over the pipe radius (diskavg), and the external temperature seen by the pipe is the circumferential average (circavg) of the surrounding temperature. Used for borehole heat exchangers, underfloor heating and mold cooling.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Pipe Wall Heat Transfer; Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("pwht1", "PipeWallHeatTransfer", 1)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Heat transfer (ht) and Heat transfer in pipes (htp or nipfl).

parameters.name: Edge selection
parameters.description: Pipe edges embedded in the heat transfer domain.

tools.notes: Verified type string PipeWallHeatTransfer (edge-level coupling). The Wall Heat Transfer node must exist on the pipe side.

tools.name: Fluid–Pipe Interaction (Multiphysics Coupling)
tools.description: Edge coupling that transfers fluid loads (internal pressure, and friction/momentum loads) from the Pipe Flow interface to the Pipe Mechanics interface, so stresses and displacements of piping systems due to flow are computed; temperature loads can be added with Heat Transfer in Pipes.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Fluid–Pipe Interaction; Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("fpipe1", "FluidPipeInteraction", 1)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Pipe flow (pfl) and Pipe mechanics (pipem).

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Pipe edges.

tools.notes: Verified type string FluidPipeInteraction (tag fpipe). Pipe Mechanics requires the Structural Mechanics Module; documentation of the coupling is in the Structural Mechanics Module guide.

tools.name: Pipe Flow Equations and Minor Loss Coefficients (Theory)
tools.description: Theory behind the Pipe Flow interfaces: cross-section-averaged continuity and momentum along the pipe with the Darcy friction factor term f_D ρ|u|u/(2 d_h), hydraulic diameter d_h = 4A/Z for noncircular sections, and lumped minor losses Δp = K ρ u²/2 at bends (0.9/0.5), valves (globe 10, angle 4.4, gate 0.2, ball 4.5, butterfly 0.6, swing check 2.5), T-junctions, contractions and expansions from standard tables.
tools.usage: Reference (Pipe Flow Module User's Guide > Theory for the Pipe Flow Interface)

parameters.name: Hydraulic diameter
parameters.description: d_h = 4A/Z.

parameters.name: Minor loss Δp
parameters.description: K ρ u² / 2 at point features.

tools.example: // Hand check: 50 m of 50 mm steel pipe at 2 m/s water, f_D ~ 0.02 -> dp = 0.02*50/0.05*1000*2^2/2 = 40 kPa
tools.notes: Minor-loss coefficients assume fully turbulent flow.
